cases.question: How did CBA's net interest margin evolve from FY21 to FY26, and what drove each phase of the journey?
gold_answer_facts: The path (full-year group NIM, bps): FY21 203 -> FY22 190 -> FY23 207 -> FY24 199 -> FY25 208 -> FY26 205

Basis trap: the FY22 deck restates the FY21 comparative to 208 (continuing operations re-presentation) versus the 203 the FY21-era documents published; a coherent narrative must note the restated basis

Phase 1, FY21-FY22 (-18 on the restated basis): the low-rate squeeze - swap/cash rates on home loan pricing -5, fixed-rate switching -6, SVR price competition -6, partly offset by funding +6; liquid asset growth -8 with minimal NII impact
Phase 2, FY23 (+17): the rising-rate recovery - funding costs +29 and replicated products/capital +12, against lending competition -21
Phase 3, FY24 (-8): deposit price competition and switching - asset pricing -6, funding costs -7, partly offset by replicating portfolio +6
Phase 4, FY25 (+9): liquids/pooled facilities unwind +7 (broadly revenue neutral) and capital/replicating +9, against deposit competition -7
Phase 5, FY26 (-3): liquids and repo growth -3 and asset pricing -5, offset by interest rate risk hedging +5; underlying NIM broadly stable

A through-line a good note names: the replicating portfolio/hedging swings from headwind (FY22) to the dominant tailwind (FY23 onward) as the cash rate cycle turned; competition is a persistent negative in every single year

required_locations.holds: FY22 12-month walk (restated 208 -> 190) and the restatement footnote

cases.trap: Six documents across three disclosure-format eras; the FY22 deck silently restates the FY21 starting point (203 vs 208); each era frames its bars differently (SVR/fixed-switching era labels vs the modern canonical set). Single-document reading yields a wrong or incoherent path; the test is consolidation into one narrative with the basis change acknowledged.
